Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 62, verses 5–8:

﴿Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you."﴾ It may have four meanings:

The first: its meaning is, "You flee from illness by means of medicine, but indeed it will meet you by the expiry of your term."

The second: "You flee from jihad by remaining behind, but indeed it will meet you by the threat (of punishment)."

The third: "You flee from it (death) by being superstitious about mentioning it, fearing its descent upon you, but indeed it will meet you with what you dislike and what you accept."

The fourth: it is "the death from which you flee" in the sense of wishing for it, when Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So wish for death﴾.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (*al-Nukat wa al-Uyun*) on surah 62, verses 9–10:**

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of God﴾. Regarding the "proceeding" (*al-sa'y*) to it, there are four opinions. The first: it is the intention in the hearts, as said by al-Hasan [al-Basri]. The second: it is the action for it, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾; this was said by Ibn Zayd. The third: it is responding to the caller, as said by al-Suddi. The fourth: walking on foot without hastening. It is mentioned that 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud used to recite *fa-amdu* [in place of *fa-s'aw*], "then proceed (*fa-amdu*) to the remembrance of God."

As for "the remembrance of God" here, there are three opinions. The first: it is the imam's admonition in the khutbah (sermon), as said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. The second: it is the time, related by al-Suddi. The third: it is the prayer, and this is the view of the majority.

The name of the day of Friday in the pre-Islamic period (*al-Jahiliyyah*) was *al-'Urubah*, because the names of the days in the Jahiliyyah were other than these names. They used to call Sunday *Awwal*, Monday *Ahwan*, Tuesday *Jubar*, Wednesday *Dubar*, Thursday *Mu'nis*, Friday *'Urubah*, and Saturday *Shiyar*. One of the people of literature recited to me:

؎ I hope to live, though my day is (one of) *Awwal*, *Ahwan*, or *Jubar*, ∗∗∗ or the one following, *Dubar*, or else my day is ∗∗∗ *Mu'nis*, or *'Urubah*, or *Shiyar*.

The first person who named it "the day of Friday" was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, because the Quraysh gathered to Ka'b on it. It was also said that it was named in Islam because people gather on it for the prayer.

﴿And leave off trading﴾: God forbade it at the time of the Friday prayer and made it unlawful during its time for one who is addressed by its obligation.

Regarding the time of the prohibition, there are two opinions. One: it is from after the zenith (*al-zawal*) until after finishing the prayer; this was said by al-Dahhak. The second: it is from the time of the call to the khutbah until finishing the prayer; this was said by al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him. As for the first adhan (call), it is an innovation (*muhdath*); 'Uthman ibn 'Affan instituted it so that people might prepare themselves for attending the khutbah when Medina had expanded and its population increased. 'Umar had ordered that the call be made in the market before the mosque, so that people would rise from their trading; when they gathered, the call was made in the mosque. So 'Uthman made it two calls in the mosque. Trade is not prohibited after this and before the khutbah. If a sale is concluded during this prohibited time, the sale is not void, although he has disobeyed God, because the prohibition is specific to a cause that relates to the two contracting parties and not to the contract itself. Ibn Hanbal, however, declared it void, adhering to the apparent sense of the prohibition.

﴿That is better for you, if you knew﴾: meaning that the prayer is better for you than buying and selling, because the prayer is lost when its time passes, whereas trade is not lost.

﴿Then when the prayer is concluded﴾: meaning when it has been performed.

﴿Disperse in the land﴾: It is related from 'Iraq ibn Malik that when he had prayed the Friday prayer, he would leave, stand at the door of the mosque, and say: "O God, I have responded to Your call, prayed Your prescribed prayer, and dispersed as You commanded me. So provide me from Your bounty, and You are the best of providers."

﴿And seek from the bounty of God﴾: Regarding this there are three opinions. The first: it is provision from buying and selling; this was said by Muqatil and al-Dahhak. The second: it is work on Saturday; this was said by Ja'far ibn Muhammad. The third: what Abu Khalaf related from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "*When the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of God*," and he said: "It is not the pursuit of worldly affairs, but rather visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of God."

The third: what Abu Khalaf related from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "*When the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of God*," and he said: "It is not the pursuit of worldly affairs, but rather visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of God."

(p-9) (p-10) (p-11)

﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it and leave you standing﴾. Salim related from Jabir, who said: "A caravan arrived while we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning during the sermon, and the people turned away toward it, and only twelve men remained, so this verse was revealed." (p-12)

al-Kalbi mentioned that the one who brought it was Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi, from al-Sham, at a time of famine and high prices, and that he had with him everything they needed of wheat, flour and other goods. He halted at Ahjar al-Zayt and beat the drum to announce his arrival to the people. They were in the Friday sermon, so they broke away toward it, and only eight men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it﴾. "Trade" refers to the goods of merchandise.

Regarding "diversion" (lahw) here, there are four interpretations:

First: it means play, said by Ibn Abbas.

Second: it is the drum, said by Mujahid.

Third: it is the flute (mizmar), said by Jabir.

Fourth: it is singing.

﴿And they leave you standing﴾ means during his sermon. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you had hastened toward it until no one remained with me, the valley would have been set ablaze with fire upon you." Allah the Exalted said ﴿they break away toward it﴾ and did not say "toward them both," because most of their breaking away was for the trade and not for the diversion.

al-Akhfash said: there is taqdim wa ta'khir (inversion of order) in the speech, and its meaning is: "And when they see a trade, they break away toward it, or a diversion." Ibn Mas'ud recited it in this way.

As for ﴿they break away﴾ (infadду), there are two meanings:

One: they went away.

The second: they scattered.

Whoever takes its meaning as "they went away" means the trade; whoever takes its meaning as "they scattered" means away from the sermon. This is the more eloquent of the two meanings, said by Qutrub, and from it is the poet's saying:

"Their gathering scattered away from every disturbance,
it remains, and it defiles the honor of the sorrowful, the frowning one."

﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade﴾ may bear two meanings:

One: what is with Allah of reward for your prayer is better than the pleasure of your diversion and the benefit of your trade.

The second: what is with Allah of your provision, which He has apportioned to you, is better than what you obtained by your breaking away for your diversion and your trade.

﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾ may bear two meanings:

One: that Allah, glory be to Him, is the best of those who provide and give.

The second: and the provision of Allah is the best of provisions.
